description: A sixth Level 1 - Math I (Physics) exam set with original questions on calculus, complex methods, series, matrices, systems, and group structure.
instructions: All main questions carry the same number of marks.
Show sufficient working to justify each answer.
Begin each main question on a new page.
label: Paper 1

questions.stem: This question concerns logarithmic differentiation, trigonometric limits, stationary points, and L'Hopital's rule.
questions.title: Calculus with functions and limits

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Differentiate \(f(x)=\ln(x^2+4x+5)\), and evaluate \(f'(0)\).

parts.answer: Rewrite the quotient as \(\frac{\tan(2x)}{\sin(5x)}=\frac{\tan(2x)}{2x}\cdot\frac{5x}{\sin(5x)}\cdot\frac{2}{5}\). The first two factors tend to \(1\), so the limit is \(2/5\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\frac{\tan(2x)}{\sin(5x)}\).

parts.answer: Use the quotient rule: \(m'(x)=\frac{2x(x^2+1)-(x^2-1)(2x)}{(x^2+1)^2}\). The numerator simplifies to \(2x[(x^2+1)-(x^2-1)]=4x\), so \(m'(x)=4x/(x^2+1)^2\). A stationary point occurs when \(4x=0\), so \(x=0\), and \(m(0)=-1\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For \(m(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x^2+1}\), find \(m'(x)\) and the stationary point.

parts.answer: The expression has form \(0/0\). Applying L'Hopital's rule once gives \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{3/(1+3x)-3}{2x}\), still \(0/0\). Applying it again gives \(\lim_{x\to0}\frac{-9/(1+3x)^2}{2}=-9/2\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Use L'Hopital's rule to evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\frac{\ln(1+3x)-3x}{x^2}\).

questions.stem: This question uses substitution, integration by parts, and partial fractions after division.
questions.title: Definite and rational integrals

parts.answer: Let \(u=\sin x\), so \(du=\cos x\,dx\). The bounds are \(u=0\) and \(u=1\). Therefore \(\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2x\cos x\,dx=\int_0^1u^2\,du=1/3\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2x\cos x\,dx\).

parts.answer: Use integration by parts with \(u=x\), \(dv=e^{-2x}dx\). Then \(du=dx\) and \(v=-e^{-2x}/2\). Thus \(\int_0^1xe^{-2x}dx=\left[-\frac{x e^{-2x}}{2}\right]_0^1+\frac12\int_0^1e^{-2x}dx\). The remaining integral is \([-e^{-2x}/2]_0^1=(1-e^{-2})/2\). Hence the value is \(-e^{-2}/2+(1-e^{-2})/4=(1-3e^{-2})/4\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^1xe^{-2x}\,dx\).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int\frac{2x^2+5x+7}{x^2+3x+2}\,dx\).

questions.stem: This question concerns complex arithmetic, powers, complex sine, and roots.
questions.title: Complex arithmetic and roots

parts.answer: Multiply by the conjugate of the denominator: \(\frac{5+i}{2-i}\cdot\frac{2+i}{2+i}=\frac{(5+i)(2+i)}{5}\). The numerator is \(10+5i+2i+i^2=9+7i\). Therefore the quotient is \(9/5+7i/5\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write \(\displaystyle \frac{5+i}{2-i}\) in the form \(a+bi\).

parts.answer: By De Moivre's theorem, \((4e^{5\pi i/6})^4=4^4e^{20\pi i/6}=256e^{10\pi i/3}\). Since \(10\pi/3\) is coterminal with \(4\pi/3\), the rectangular form is \(256(\cos(4\pi/3)+i\sin(4\pi/3))=-128-128\sqrt3\,i\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use De Moivre's theorem to find \((4e^{5\pi i/6})^4\) in rectangular form.

parts.answer: Using \(\sin z=(e^{iz}-e^{-iz})/(2i)\), put \(z=ib\). Then \(e^{iz}=e^{-b}\) and \(e^{-iz}=e^b\). Hence \(\sin(ib)=\frac{e^{-b}-e^b}{2i}=i\frac{e^b-e^{-b}}{2}=i\sinh b\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using \(\sin z=\frac{e^{iz}-e^{-iz}}{2i}\), show that \(\sin(ib)=i\sinh b\).

parts.answer: Write \(-16i=16e^{-i\pi/2}\). The fourth roots have modulus \(16^{1/4}=2\) and arguments \((-\pi/2+2k\pi)/4=-\pi/8+k\pi/2\), for \(k=0,1,2,3\). Thus the roots are \(2e^{i(-\pi/8+k\pi/2)}\), \(k=0,1,2,3\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find all fourth roots of \(-16i\), giving the roots in exponential form.

questions.stem: This question uses the term test, integral test, root test, and endpoint testing.
questions.title: Choosing convergence tests

parts.answer: The terms satisfy \(\frac{3n+2}{2n+1}\to3/2\), not \(0\). Since a necessary condition for series convergence is that the terms tend to \(0\), the series diverges by the term test.
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the term test to classify \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{3n+2}{2n+1}\).

parts.answer: Use \(f(x)=1/(x\ln x)\), positive and decreasing for \(x>1\). Then \(\int_2^R\frac{dx}{x\ln x}=\ln(\ln R)-\ln(\ln2)\), which tends to infinity as \(R\to\infty\). By the integral test, the series diverges.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the integral test to classify \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n\ln n}\).

parts.answer: Let \(a_n=((3n-1)/(4n+5))^n\). The root test gives \(\sqrt[n]{a_n}=\frac{3n-1}{4n+5}\to3/4\). Since \(3/4<1\), the series converges.
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the root test to determine whether \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{3n-1}{4n+5}\right)^n\) converges.

parts.answer: The ratio test on absolute values gives the interior condition \(|x-1|/2<1\), so \(-1<x<3\). At \(x=3\), the series is \(\sum1/n^2\), which converges. At \(x=-1\), the series is \(\sum(-1)^n/n^2\), which converges absolutely. Therefore the interval of convergence is \([-1,3]\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(x-1)^n}{n^2 2^n}\).

questions.section: Section E: Taylor Series and Matrices
questions.stem: This question combines Taylor approximation with orthogonal and skew-symmetric matrix structure.
questions.title: Taylor bounds and matrix structure

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the cubic Taylor polynomial for \(e^{x/2}\) about \(0\), and use it to approximate \(e^{0.1}\).

parts.answer: The fourth derivative is \(f^{(4)}(x)=e^{x/2}/16\). On \(0\le x\le0.2\), use the simple bound \(e^{x/2}<2\), so \(M=1/8\). Then \(|R_3(0.2)|\le\frac{1/8}{4!}(0.2)^4=\frac{0.0016}{192}\approx0.00000833\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Give a Lagrange remainder bound for the approximation in part (a).

parts.answer: The columns of \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{pmatrix}\) are \((a,b)^T\) and \((b,-a)^T\). Their dot product is \(ab-ab=0\), so they are orthogonal. Their squared lengths are both \(a^2+b^2\). Therefore \(Q\) is orthogonal exactly when \(a^2+b^2=1\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the condition on real \(a\) and \(b\) for \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{pmatrix}\) to be orthogonal.

parts.answer: If \(S\) is real skew-symmetric, then \(S^T=-S\). For any real vector \(\mathbf x\), the scalar \(\mathbf x^TS\mathbf x\) equals its transpose: \((\mathbf x^TS\mathbf x)^T=\mathbf x^TS^T\mathbf x=-\mathbf x^TS\mathbf x\). Hence it is equal to its negative, so \(\mathbf x^TS\mathbf x=0\). This shows skew-symmetric matrices produce no quadratic self-term.
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Prove that \(\mathbf x^TS\mathbf x=0\) for every real vector \(\mathbf x\) when \(S\) is real skew-symmetric.

questions.stem:
Consider the parameter-dependent system
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+2y+z&=1,\\
2x+5y+3z&=4,\\
x+3y+az&=b.
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.title: A parameter-dependent linear system

parts.answer: Use row operations. From the augmented matrix, \(R_2-2R_1\) gives \((0,1,1|2)\), and \(R_3-R_1\) gives \((0,1,a-1|b-1)\). Subtracting these rows gives \((0,0,a-2|b-3)\). Therefore the coefficient matrix is invertible exactly when \(a-2\ne0\), so \(a\ne2\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the values of \(a\) for which the system has a unique solution.

parts.answer: When \(a=2\), the last row becomes \((0,0,0|b-3)\). If \(b\ne3\), this is a contradiction, so there is no solution. If \(b=3\), the last row is \(0=0\), so the system is consistent with a free variable and has infinitely many solutions.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Classify the non-unique cases.

parts.answer: For \(a=2\), \(b=3\), the reduced equations are \(x+2y+z=1\) and \(y+z=2\). Let \(z=t\). Then \(y=2-t\), and \(x=1-2(2-t)-t=t-3\). Thus \((x,y,z)=(t-3,2-t,t)\), where \(t\in\mathbb R\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For the infinitely many solution case, write the solution set in parameter form.

parts.answer: For \(a=3\), \(b=5\), the last row gives \(z=2\). Then \(y+z=2\) gives \(y=0\). The first equation gives \(x+0+2=1\), so \(x=-1\). The solution is \((-1,0,2)\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Solve the system for \(a=3\) and \(b=5\).

questions.section: Section G: Groups and Matrix Structure
questions.stem: For each real number \(t\), let \(M_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\). Let \(G=\{M_t:t\in\mathbb R\}\), with operation matrix multiplication.
questions.title: A matrix group under multiplication

parts.answer: For \(s,t\in\mathbb R\), multiply the matrices: \(M_sM_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&s\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&s+t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=M_{s+t}\). Since \(s+t\in\mathbb R\), the product \(M_sM_t\) lies in \(G\). Therefore \(G\) is closed under the operation.
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Compute \(M_sM_t\), and use the multiplication rule to show closure in \(G\).

parts.answer: The identity element is \(M_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\), because \(M_0M_t=M_{0+t}=M_t\) and \(M_tM_0=M_{t+0}=M_t\). The inverse of \(M_t\) is \(M_{-t}\), since \(M_tM_{-t}=M_{t-t}=M_0\) and \(M_{-t}M_t=M_{-t+t}=M_0\). Since \(-t\in\mathbb R\), this inverse lies in \(G\).
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Identify the identity element and find the inverse of \(M_t\) in \(G\).

parts.answer: Matrix multiplication is associative for all compatible matrices, so associativity is inherited by \(G\). Part (a) gives closure, and part (b) gives an identity and inverses inside \(G\). Therefore \(G\) is a group under matrix multiplication. Also \(M_sM_t=M_{s+t}=M_{t+s}=M_tM_s\), so the group is abelian.
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Conclude that \(G\) is a group under matrix multiplication and decide whether \(G\) is abelian.

parts.answer: The subset \(H\) is non-empty because \(M_0\in H\). If \(M_m,M_n\in H\), where \(m,n\in\mathbb Z\), then \(M_n^{-1}=M_{-n}\) and \(M_mM_n^{-1}=M_mM_{-n}=M_{m-n}\). Since \(m-n\in\mathbb Z\), this product lies in \(H\). By the subgroup test, \(H\) is a subgroup of \(G\).
parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Let \(H=\{M_n:n\in\mathbb Z\}\). Prove that \(H\) is a subgroup of \(G\).
